status.comment: C 2026-07-25: [package].bridge parses in vibe-core and all three composed mechanisms ship; motivation, rejected and out-of-scope facts stay spec-stage; fact grain 2026-07-24

p.status-line: **Status: IMPLEMENTED** (specified 2026-06-24 in an owner-requested design session; verified against the tree 2026-07-25 by the spec-actualization campaign). The umbrella's own addition — `[package].bridge`, defaulting to false — parses in `vibe-core` with a doctest, and the three mechanisms it composes all ship: [PROP-020](../vibe-workspace/PROP-020-install-hooks.xml) install hooks, [PROP-021](PROP-021-submodule-sources.xml) submodule sources, [PROP-022](../vibe-workspace/PROP-022-materialization-modes.xml) materialization modes — so every composition law recorded here describes live machinery. It still adds little of its own: a flag and a packaging convention. Each mechanism stands alone; bridges are where they line up.

p.related: **Related:** [PROP-002](PROP-002-decentralized-registry.xml) (a bridge is an ordinary package + identity), [PROP-008](PROP-008-qualified-naming.xml) (the maintainer's group, distinct from the upstream author), [PROP-015 §2.6](../vibe-mcp/PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml#skill) + [PROP-015 #skill-include](../vibe-mcp/PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml#skill-include) (projecting a skill out of the bridged subtree, selectively), [PROP-000 §16](../../common/PROP-000.xml) (the installable kinds a bridge still belongs to).

problem.title: 1.1 The problem — good work that nobody packaged

facts.unpackaged-work: People publish skills and projects to GitHub / GitVerse without ever making a vibevm package — out of disinterest, or because their repo's layout has nothing to do with vibevm conventions.
facts.unreachable: That work is then unreachable through `vibe install`, and the original author has no incentive to change.

facts.BRIDGE-DEF: A **bridge package** closes the gap without the author's involvement: a *maintainer* volunteers to steward someone else's repository and publishes an ordinary vibevm package that **wraps** it.
facts.BRIDGE-MEANS: The bridge brings the foreign repo in by one of git's two means and, where needed, runs hooks to shape it into something vibevm can consume.

what.title: 1.2 What this is — a thin convention over three mechanisms

p.thin-convention: A bridge is not a new kind of package or a new subsystem. It is:

facts.conv-embedded-content: carrying the foreign repo as **vendored** content or a **submodule** ([PROP-021](PROP-021-submodule-sources.xml)),
facts.conv-in-place: optionally **materialised** as `in-place` when the upstream is a giant ([PROP-022](../vibe-workspace/PROP-022-materialization-modes.xml)),
facts.conv-skill-projection: with any skill projected selectively from the bridged subtree ([PROP-015 #skill-include](../vibe-mcp/PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml#skill-include)).

p.plus-flag: …plus one flag that says "this is a bridge."

flag.title: 2.1 A bridge is marked by a flag, not a kind

facts.BRIDGE-FLAG: `[package].bridge = true` marks a package as a bridge.
facts.FLAG-NOT-KIND: It does **not** change the package's `kind` (a bridged skill is still a `feat`/`tool` as appropriate) or its identity.
facts.FLAG-JOBS: The flag is metadata with two jobs: it documents that the package's substantive content is *foreign* (stewarded, not authored, by the maintainer), and it is the hook the registry/UI uses to surface provenance (§2.4).
facts.FLAG-DEFAULT: Default `false`; the overwhelming majority of packages are not bridges.

p.TWO-CLASSES: A bridge embeds the upstream repo one of two ways:

facts.CLASS-VENDORED: **Vendored ("git in git")** — the maintainer copied the upstream tree into the package and committed it. This needs **none** of PROP-021/022 machinery: it is plain files in a `snapshot` package. A vendored bridge is therefore the cheapest case — the flag (§2.1) plus, if the layout needs shaping, hooks.
facts.CLASS-SUBMODULE: **Submodule-backed** — the package references the upstream via a git submodule ([PROP-021](PROP-021-submodule-sources.xml)), fetched on install and updated on update, so the bridge tracks upstream without re-vendoring.

p.CLASS-TRADEOFF: The maintainer chooses per trade-off: vendored is self-contained and frozen; submodule-backed stays current but depends on upstream remaining reachable.

p.COMPOSE-OPTIONAL: A bridge is the point where the three orthogonal mechanisms compose, but it mandates none of them:

facts.OPT-NO-HOOKS: a bridge **without hooks** is valid (the upstream layout already fits);
facts.OPT-NO-SUBMODULE: a bridge **without a submodule** is valid (vendored);
facts.OPT-NO-IN-PLACE: a bridge **without `in-place`** is the norm (`in-place` is only for giant upstreams).

facts.CANONICAL-FULL-CASE: The canonical full case — submodule-backed + `pre-install` hook to shape the tree + selective skill projection — is the union of the four specs, but each piece is independently usable outside any bridge.
facts.FOUR-SPECS-WHY: This is why they are four specs and four test sets, not one (the owner's orthogonality requirement).

facts.MAINTAINER-VS-AUTHOR: The bridge's **maintainer** is distinct from the upstream **author**.
facts.GROUP-PROVENANCE: The package's `group` ([PROP-008](PROP-008-qualified-naming.xml)) is the maintainer's namespace; the upstream is recorded as provenance (its repository URL, and — where applicable — the `describes` PURL the descriptor already supports, [PROP-015 §0](../vibe-mcp/PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml)).
facts.PROVENANCE-VISIBLE: A consumer can therefore always see *who stewards this* and *what it wraps*.
facts.SKILL-VIA-INCLUDE: A skill that lives inside the bridged subtree is projected through the normal skill machinery, using the `include` selector ([PROP-015 #skill-include](../vibe-mcp/PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml#skill-include)) to pick the relevant files out of an upstream tree full of unrelated content.

facts.REJ-BRIDGE-KIND: **A `bridge` package kind** (a kind of its own beside the §4.1 register) — rejected: the kinds describe *what the package is for*; "bridge" describes *where its content came from*. They are orthogonal axes, so bridge is a flag, not a kind. (The reasoning survives the register later growing `mcp` — that kind, too, says what a package is FOR.)

facts.OOS-AUTO-CONVERSION: **Automatic conversion of foreign layouts** into vibevm conventions — bridges shape upstream with explicit, maintainer-written hooks, not inferred magic.
facts.OOS-SECURITY-SCAN: **Security scanning of wrapped third-party code** — the LLM "antivirus" is the same far-backlog item as for hooks ([PROP-020 §4](../vibe-workspace/PROP-020-install-hooks.xml#out-of-scope)); a bridge's trust posture is its maintainer plus the hook allow-list/consent gate, an explicitly accepted risk for now.
facts.OOS-LICENSE-TRACKING: **License / legal provenance tracking** of wrapped upstreams — beyond the recorded URL/PURL, no compliance machinery is specified here.

facts.ACC-FLAG-PARSES: `[package].bridge` parses as a boolean, defaults `false`, and does not alter `kind` or identity.
facts.ACC-VENDORED-PLAIN: A vendored bridge installs as a plain `snapshot` package (flag + optional hooks), with no submodule/materialization machinery engaged.
facts.ACC-SUBMODULE-FULL: A submodule-backed bridge fetches upstream ([PROP-021](PROP-021-submodule-sources.xml)), runs declared hooks ([PROP-020](../vibe-workspace/PROP-020-install-hooks.xml)), and projects its skill via the `include` selector.
facts.ACC-PROVENANCE: Provenance (maintainer group + upstream URL/PURL) is recoverable for a bridge package.
